stem: Which constitutional body has visitorial powers over jails, prisons and detention facilities?

choices.text: Commission on Audit
Commission on Human Rights
Civil Service Commission
Commission on Elections

explanation: Article XIII, Section 18(4) assigns this visitorial function to the CHR. Financial audit, personnel administration and election administration do not substitute for that specific mandate.

choices.text: Peaceful assembly and petition for redress
Travel and choice of abode
Bail and speedy trial
Association and non-impairment of contracts

explanation: The residents assemble peacefully and petition the government about a grievance. The other pairs concern different activities and do not describe both acts.

stem: Article XIV expressly guarantees academic freedom in which institutions?

choices.text: Only public elementary schools
Only government research offices
All institutions of higher learning
All offices offering staff orientation

explanation: Article XIV, Section 5(2) identifies all institutions of higher learning. The guarantee is not limited to public institutions or extended by this wording to every training office.

stem: A resettlement team adequately consults the families who will move but says the receiving community has no part in consultation. Which assessment follows Article XIII, Section 10?

choices.text: Consultation is required only after relocation
The moving families alone satisfy the express requirement
The receiving community alone should have been consulted
Both the dwellers and the receiving community must be adequately consulted

explanation: The second paragraph expressly includes the dwellers and the communities where they will be relocated. Consulting one group does not remove the other; after-the-fact notice is not the required prior consultation.

stem: A housing proposal correctly seeks affordable homes for underprivileged citizens, but its summary says the constitutional programme disregards all small property owners. What correction is needed?

choices.text: The programme must also respect small property-owner rights
The housing programme gives small owners an absolute veto over every proposed project
The provision protects small owners only if they are also prospective beneficiaries
Respect for small owners is required only after construction has been completed

explanation: Article XIII, Section 9 expressly requires respect for small property-owner rights during implementation. It does not phrase that safeguard as an absolute veto, limit it to future beneficiaries, or postpone it until after construction.

stem: An applicant says the constitutional right to choose a course of study requires admission even when fair, reasonable and equitable academic requirements are unmet. Which reply is accurate?

choices.text: Course choice is absolute once an applicant is a citizen
The right is expressly subject to those requirements
Only private institutions may impose those requirements
Admission requirements are allowed, but academic requirements after admission are excluded

explanation: Article XIV, Section 5(3) protects course/profession choice subject to fair, reasonable and equitable admission and academic requirements. It does not exempt citizens, limit the condition to private schools, or exclude later academic requirements.

stem: A proposed scholarship summary excludes all students in private schools solely because the Constitution mentions public education elsewhere. Which correction follows Article XIV, Section 2(3)?

choices.text: Private-school students can benefit only from loans, never grants
The provision covers only teachers rather than students
Deserving students in both public and private schools are contemplated
All private-school students are automatically entitled to every scholarship

explanation: Section 2(3) contemplates scholarship grants and related incentives for deserving students in both sectors, especially the underprivileged. It does not guarantee every applicant every award or exclude grants from the private sector.

stem: Consider only Article XIV, Section 3(3). A public high school proposes religious instruction during regular class hours. Plan R has written parental options and instructors approved by the relevant religious authorities, but charges the Government an additional instructor fee. Plan S has the same written options and approved instructors, with no additional government cost. Plan T has no additional government cost and approved instructors, but relies only on oral parental requests. Which plans satisfy all these express conditions?

choices.text: R and S, because approval cures the fee
S alone, because both writing and no additional government cost are required
S and T, because an oral option substitutes for writing
R alone, because additional payment is required for approved instructors

explanation: R fails the no-additional-cost condition; T fails the written-option condition. S meets writing, religious-authority designation/approval and cost requirements. Both S-containing distractors preserve one correct condition but wrongly waive another.

stem: RA 9710 seeks substantive equality of women and men. Which focus best captures this policy?

choices.text: Identical wording of every rule regardless of barriers
Permanent separation of all educational standards
Equal opportunities, access to resources and development outcomes
Replacement of every individual assessment with a fixed entitlement

explanation: Section 2 addresses opportunities, resources and development results in light of unequal structures. Identical wording alone may retain barriers, while permanent unequal standards and automatic universal entitlements do not define substantive equality.

choices.text: When their objectives have been achieved
When their first annual budget is released
Whenever they benefit a previously disadvantaged group
Only when all ordinary public services are discontinued

explanation: Section 4(j) links discontinuation to achieving the measures’ objectives. A first budget or the fact that a measure addresses disadvantage is not the stated endpoint.

A land-registration branch
A customs clearance post
A Violence Against Women Desk

explanation: Section 9(d) specifies a VAW Desk in every barangay. The other institutions have unrelated functions and are not that statutory mechanism.

stem: A training rule is worded identically for everyone. Evidence shows it denies women access because of a sex-based disadvantage that the rule makes no provision to address. A manager says identical wording alone rules out discrimination. Under RA 9710, what is the best assessment?

choices.text: Discrimination requires an expressly hostile written statement
A generally applicable measure can still be discriminatory through its effects
Discrimination is defined only for married women
A training rule cannot be an administrative measure

explanation: Section 4(b) includes direct and indirect restrictions, including generally applicable measures that fail to address sex/gender disadvantages and thereby deny rights or opportunities. Neutral wording alone is not conclusive, and marital status is not an exclusion.

stem: A school admits women to technical courses but keeps textbooks portraying all technical work as exclusively male. It claims admission alone completes its obligations under RA 9710, Section 13(a). Which response is best?

choices.text: The provision also addresses gender stereotypes in educational materials
Equal admission is sufficient unless a textbook expressly prohibits enrolment
The stereotype provisions govern teachers’ conduct but exclude printed curricula
Revision of stereotypes is required only in materials written by government employees

explanation: Section 13(a) covers stereotypes and images in educational materials and curricula, alongside gender-sensitive language. Its content duties are not conditioned on an express enrolment ban, limited to teachers’ conduct, or restricted by authors’ employment.

stem: After a flood, an assistance plan for women provides food on the first day but excludes recovery and rehabilitation on the ground that protection ends with initial relief. Which interpretation of RA 9710, Section 10 is strongest?

choices.text: The section applies only to evacuation-centre buildings
Recovery is covered only if relief was delayed
Protection also reaches recovery, rehabilitation and reconstruction
The section treats health services as unrelated to crisis response

explanation: Section 10 extends protection through relief, recovery, rehabilitation and reconstruction and identifies wider support needs. Immediate food assistance therefore does not exhaust the section’s reach.

stem: Apply RA 9710’s definition of temporary special measures. All three measures aim to accelerate de facto equality. P retains common standards and stops when its objective is achieved. Q retains common standards but is designed to continue permanently after its objective is achieved. R stops when its objective is achieved but maintains unequal separate standards as its consequence. Which measures meet both the standards safeguard and the endpoint rule?

choices.text: P and Q
P alone
P and R
Q and R

explanation: Section 4(j), with 4(g), forbids maintaining unequal/separate standards and requires discontinuation when objectives are achieved. P satisfies both. Q satisfies the standards condition but fails the endpoint; R satisfies the endpoint but fails the standards condition. One condition alone leaves a P-containing rival.

stem: Under RA 9710, Section 14, a tournament open to both sexes uses male and female divisions in the same sports category. It offers a smaller prize to women winners. Separately, a school gives women 40% of athletic scholarships although women make up 60% of its students. Considering only the equal-prize rule and pro rata scholarship rule, which paired correction is supported?

choices.text: Equalize prizes in that category; align women’s scholarship representation with their student-population share
Equalize prizes in that category; use a 50% scholarship share regardless of population
Keep the divided prizes; align scholarships with the student-population share
Keep the divided prizes; use the women’s share of tournament entrants for scholarships

explanation: Section 14 forbids differing prize amount/value in the same category when the event is open to both sexes and divided by sex. It separately bases women’s athletic-scholarship representation on the school’s women-student proportion. A fixed 50% or tournament-entry denominator substitutes a different rule.

choices.text: A stationary factory stack
A fuel-powered delivery bus
A fixed warehouse wall
A roadside monitoring instrument

explanation: RA 8749 Section 5(m) describes a fuel-propelled vehicle principally carrying people or property. The stack is stationary, the wall is not a source of that type, and the monitor measures air.

choices.text: Certificate of conformity
Octane rating
Ambient air quality
Source emission

explanation: Section 5(d) distinguishes general pollution in a broad area from source discharge measurements. The other terms concern vehicle certification, fuel properties or a source release.

choices.text: Airsheds must be identical to electoral districts
Only population size may determine an airshed
Municipal boundaries eliminate the need for coordination
Designation can reflect shared atmospheric conditions and pollution interchange

explanation: Section 9 uses climate, meteorology, topology and pollutant interchange/diffusion, among other grounds, and calls for common planning. It does not fix airsheds to electoral or municipal boundaries.

stem: A plant redesigns a process so it generates less air pollution, rather than relying only on equipment that captures pollutants after generation. Which policy emphasis in RA 8749 is most directly illustrated?

choices.text: Giving primary attention to pollution prevention
Showing that the Act ranks end-of-pipe control above process changes
Showing that prevention applies only when no capture technology is available
Replacing accountability for adverse impacts with voluntary process improvements

explanation: Section 3(c) gives primary focus to prevention while retaining comprehensive management; Section 3(e) separately retains accountability. The redesign illustrates prevention without making it conditional on the absence of capture equipment or removing accountability.

stem: An air-quality programme publishes technical figures but bars residents from contributing to planning or monitoring. Which policy element remains unfulfilled despite publication?

choices.text: Octane labelling alone
Participation of an informed and active public
A requirement that residents replace all inspectors
A rule limiting consultation to manufacturers

explanation: Section 3(d) couples information/education with public participation in planning and monitoring. Publication addresses only part of that policy, and participation is not equivalent to replacing technical inspectors.

stem: One factory reduces its measured emissions. Other sources and weather conditions are not studied. Which conclusion avoids confusing source and ambient measurements?

choices.text: Every location in the town must now have cleaner air
The factory’s emissions cannot have changed without a new airshed
The factory result alone does not establish the whole area’s ambient change
Ambient air quality means the factory’s permitted discharge rate

explanation: Sections 5(d) and 5(h) distinguish broad-area quality and a source release. A source reduction is relevant but cannot alone establish a broad-area result with other influences unknown.

stem: An airshed crosses provincial boundaries with shared atmospheric conditions. Under RA 8749, Section 9, proposal L has a common action plan but a Board of governors only. Proposal M has the specified DENR-Secretary-led multi-sectoral Board but no common airshed action plan. Proposal N has both that Board and a common action plan. Which proposals satisfy both the stated planning and Board requirements?

choices.text: N alone
L and N
M and N
L and M

explanation: Section 9 requires a common action plan as well as the Secretary-led Board with local officials, agencies, people’s organisations, NGOs and the private sector. L meets planning but lacks the specified Board; M has the Board but lacks common planning; N meets both. Either rule alone leaves another proposal plausible.

stem: A lesson makes two claims about RA 8749: I. A listed naturally occurring atmospheric gas can never be an air pollutant, whatever its concentration. II. A vehicle’s tailpipe reading is itself the broad-area ambient air-quality measurement. Which correction best preserves the distinctions in Sections 5(a), 5(d) and 5(h)?

choices.text: Reject I because normal concentrations matter; accept II because both are air measurements
Accept I because natural origin is decisive; reject II because a tailpipe is a source
Accept both because the Act uses one definition for all gases and measurements
Reject I because the exclusion refers to natural/normal concentrations; reject II because source emissions and ambient quality differ

explanation: Section 5(a)’s exclusion for listed gases is qualified by natural or normal concentration, so origin is not an unlimited exemption. Sections 5(d) and 5(h) separately distinguish broad-area ambient conditions from source emissions. Each single-correction alternative overlooks the other distinction.

Aquifer
Airshed
Discharge permit

explanation: Section 4(a) defines the water-transmitting underground rock layer as an aquifer. Effluent is an outflow, an airshed concerns air, and a permit is an authorization.

A beneficial-use inventory
An effluent standard
A list of recreational users

explanation: Section 4(n) defines an effluent standard as legal limits on discharge parameters. A vulnerability map or use inventory describes different conditions and does not itself state that source limit.

Only underground dumping can count as discharge
A release counts only after a fish kill has been proved
Discharge is defined solely as evaporation into air

explanation: Section 4(j) expressly includes land pathways into water. Direct pouring, a fish kill or an underground location is not a necessary part of that definition.

It excludes civil liability for non-land-based sources
Its primary focus makes all other sources legally irrelevant
It covers water-quality management in all water bodies, with relevant standards and liabilities enforced irrespective of source

explanation: Section 3 distinguishes all-water-body coverage and source-neutral enforcement from the primary emphasis on land-based abatement. Priority is not the same as exclusive coverage.

The map indicates susceptibility, not a completed contamination finding
The map guarantees the well is safe until a spill is reported

Both are beneficial only when the water is part of a municipal supply
Both domestic and recreational uses are contemplated
Recreation is a beneficial use only when combined with commercial fisheries

stem: A factory first changes its process to use less hazardous input and generate less wastewater. It later removes pollutants already spilled into a creek and restores the affected area. Adviser J calls both activities cleanup because both improve the environment. Adviser K calls the first cleaner production and the second cleanup, while warning that the second does not erase the need for prevention. Which assessment best follows RA 9275?

choices.text: The first is cleaner production and the second is cleanup; completing cleanup does not remove the prevention focus
The first is cleaner production and the second is cleanup; completing cleanup makes prevention inapplicable to the factory
Both are cleaner production because prevention includes removal of an existing spill; the prevention focus remains
The first is cleanup and the second is cleaner production; completing either removes the need for the other

explanation: Section 4(f) describes integrated preventive cleaner production, whereas 4(g) describes removal/restoration after discharge. Section 2(g) independently retains the prevention focus. The alternatives retaining both correct labels still differ on whether prevention continues; the others conflate stages or reverse them.

stem: Assume a coastal vessel releases waste and a warehouse releases waste onto land where it may drain into a stream. A memo says the vessel falls outside RA 9275 because land-based sources are prioritised, while the warehouse is outside the definition of discharge because its release first touches soil. Which review correctly evaluates both claims?

choices.text: Both exclusions fail: priority is not exclusive coverage, and the land-to-water pathway is included
The vessel exclusion fails, but the warehouse exclusion is valid until liquid directly enters the stream
The warehouse exclusion fails, but the vessel exclusion follows from the land-based priority
Both exclusions are valid whenever a direct river outfall is absent

explanation: Section 3 applies relevant standards and liability provisions irrespective of source despite the land-source priority. Section 4(j) includes release onto land from which material might drain to water. Each claim incorrectly turns a qualification into an exclusion.

National culture is to be preserved, enriched and allowed dynamic evolution through unity in diversity

explanation: Article XIV, Section 14 combines preservation, enrichment and dynamic evolution with unity in diversity and free expression. Protecting historic objects does not require freezing culture or abolishing diversity.

stem: A language-policy chart labels Spanish and Arabic as compulsory national official languages, while calling regional languages irrelevant to instruction. Which revision follows Article XIV, Section 7?

Replace Filipino with Spanish as the sole official language
Treat every regional language as the sole national language
Describe regional languages as auxiliary official/media-of-instruction languages in their regions and Spanish/Arabic promotion as voluntary and optional

explanation: Section 7 gives the regional languages auxiliary status in their regions and provides voluntary, optional promotion of Spanish and Arabic. It names Filipino and, until otherwise provided by law, English for communication/instruction as official languages.

stem: An ethics manual lists four proposed summaries of RA 6713’s nationalism and patriotism norm. Which one most closely follows Section 4(A)(f)?

choices.text: Encourage appreciation of country and people, use of locally produced resources and technology, and protection of national sovereignty
Encourage local products only when bought for personal use, while excluding government work from that norm
Protect sovereignty but prefer a party’s interests whenever the party speaks in the name of national unity
Encourage local technology but make loyalty to the Republic conditional on the employee’s regional affiliation

explanation: Section 4(A)(f) combines loyalty to the Republic/Filipino people, appreciation of country/people, use of local resources/technology and protection of sovereignty. The alternatives retain one element while adding an unstated personal-use, party-interest or regional-loyalty restriction.

stem: An agency redesigns its service guide under RA 6713’s responsiveness-to-the-public norm. Which interpretation best combines the information and procedure duties?

choices.text: Use clear language, but retain unnecessary procedures whenever applicants can read them
Use clear understandable information and simplified procedures that avoid red tape
Simplify procedures, but provide explanations only to applicants represented by counsel
Make the guide understandable, but treat consultation as required only after all decisions are final

explanation: Section 4(A)(e) calls for clear understandable information, openness/consultation and simplified systematic procedures free of red tape. Clear wording does not justify unnecessary steps or replace openness, and the norm does not restrict information to represented applicants.

stem: A training note proposes that an elected party leader’s instructions may displace public accountability. Which replacement most accurately states RA 6713’s commitment-to-democracy norm?

choices.text: Uphold accountability except when party instructions are issued during an elected term
Put civilian authority first, but treat personal loyalty as superior to loyalty to country
Uphold the Constitution, accountability and civilian supremacy, with country above persons or party
Put country above party only in elections; apply the reverse order in ordinary administration

explanation: Section 4(A)(g) joins constitutional loyalty, accountability and civilian supremacy with country above persons/party. None of those commitments is made election-only or suspended for instructions issued by an elected leader.

stem: Consider only the ownership, control/administration and alien-enrolment conditions in Article XIV, Section 4(2). These ordinary schools are outside every stated exception, no law requires higher Filipino equity, and all unmentioned conditions are satisfied. School I has 60% Filipino capital, Filipino control/administration, and 30 alien students among 90 enrolled. School J has 65% Filipino capital, Filipino control/administration, and 31 alien students among 90. School K has 70% Filipino capital, alien control/administration, and 20 alien students among 90. Which schools meet all three conditions?

choices.text: I and J
I alone
I and K
J and K

explanation: The constitutional minimum is 60% Filipino capital; control and administration must be vested in Filipino citizens; aliens may comprise no more than one third of enrolment outside the exceptions. I meets all three, including30/90 exactly one third. J exceeds the enrolment ceiling at 31/90 despite adequate equity/control. K meets equity/enrolment but fails citizen control. Checking either failed condition alone leaves an I-containing rival.
